summary: Feed s145_double is degraded: NDR receives 9.1% duplicate packets and 18.6% one-way TCP sessions (29/156), breaking bidirectional session reconstruction required for NDR detection.

findings.root_cause: Same packets arriving via multiple SPAN/TAP paths aggregated without deduplication on the packet broker. 223 of 2459 packets (9.1%) exceed 5% threshold, typical of overlapping SPANs or dual-sided TAP aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate processing, inflates flow/packet counters, skews analytics and can cause false-positive detections and missed true positives due to state confusion.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within short window before delivery to NDR, restoring accurate counts without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker not aggregating both directions of TCP sessions to this NDR port - likely asymmetric routing with separate capture points or hash-based load-balancing splitting client->server and server->client to different tools.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions for TCP reassembly, session state, and attack detection. With 18.6% one-way sessions, NDR cannot reconstruct flows, misses lateral movement, C2, and exploit detection and generates incomplete flow records.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate/correlate both directions using bidirectional 5-tuple hashing so each TCP session's forward and reverse packets go to the same NDR port.
